info.title: Kahuna.Server
info.description: Kahuna server node — distributed key-value store, lock manager and sequencer. Run `kahuna-server` to start a standalone node.

options.name: --host
options.description:
(Default: *) Host to bind
incoming connections to

options.name: --http-ports
options.description:
Ports to bind incoming
HTTP connections to

options.name: --https-ports
options.description:
Ports to bind incoming
HTTPs connections to

options.name: --grpc-cleartext-ports
options.description:
Ports to bind cleartext
HTTP/2 (h2c) connections
to. gRPC-only: these
listeners speak HTTP/2
without TLS and reject
HTTP/1.1, so REST clients
must use the http/https
ports instead. A
standalone node defaults
to 2072; a node joining a
cluster binds nothing
unless this option is
given

options.name: --https-certificate
options.description:
Path to the HTTPs
certificate

options.name: --https-certificate-password
options.description:
(Default: ) Password of
the HTTPs certificate

options.name: --disable-dashboard
options.description:
Do not serve the browser
operator dashboard at the
HTTP root

options.name: --dashboard-refresh-seconds
options.description:
(Default: 5) How often
the dashboard polls this
node, in seconds (1-300)

options.name: --storage
options.description:
(Default: rocksdb)
Storage (rocksdb, sqlite,
memory)

options.name: --storage-path
options.description: Storage path

options.name: --storage-revision
options.description: Storage revision

options.name: --wal-storage
options.description:
(Default: rocksdb) WAL
storage (rocksdb, sqlite,

options.name: --wal-path
options.description: WAL path

options.name: --wal-revision
options.description:
(Default: v1) WAL
revision

options.name: --wal-sync-writes
options.description:
Use synchronous durable
WAL writes (default:
enabled)

options.name: --disable-wal-sync-writes
options.description:
Disable synchronous
durable WAL writes for
faster non-critical
test/local runs

options.name: --rocksdb-shared-memory
options.description:
Share one RocksDB block
cache + write-buffer
manager between the
KV/locks backend and the
Raft WAL (requires both
storage and wal-storage =
rocksdb). Default:
disabled

options.name: --rocksdb-shared-memory-budget-mb
options.description:
(Default: 320) Total
shared RocksDB
block-cache budget in MiB
(memtable sub-budget
lives inside it)

options.name: --rocksdb-shared-memtable-budget-mb
options.description:
(Default: 128) Shared
RocksDB memtable
sub-budget in MiB,
cost-charged into the
shared cache (must be <=
budget)

options.name: --disable-rocksdb-direct-reads
options.description:
Disable direct-I/O reads
(default: enabled) and
use buffered reads backed
by the OS page cache

options.name: --rocksdb-statistics
options.description:
Enable RocksDB statistics
collection and periodic
LOG dumps (adds
per-operation overhead;
for tuning/diagnosis).
Default: disabled

options.name: --initial-cluster
options.description:
Initial cluster
configuration for static
discovery

options.name: --join-existing
options.description:
(Default: false) Join a
running cluster as a new
node using
--initial-cluster as the
seed list. When false
(default) the node boots
via static discovery.

options.name: --graceful-leave-on-shutdown
options.description:
(Default: false) On
planned shutdown, commit
a RemoveMember so the
roster shrinks
immediately rather than
waiting for SWIM
eviction. Default false;
do not enable on rolling
restarts.

options.name: --initial-cluster-partitions
options.description:
(Default: 3) Initial
cluster number of
partitions

options.name: --raft-nodename
options.description:
Unique name to identify
the node in the cluster

options.name: --raft-nodeid
options.description:
Unique id to identify the
node in the cluster

options.name: --raft-host
options.description:
(Default: localhost) Host
to listen for Raft
consensus and replication
requests

options.name: --raft-port
options.description:
(Default: 2070) Port to
bind incoming Raft

options.name: --locks-workers
options.description:
(Default: 0) Number of
lock ephemeral/consistent
workers (0 = auto-size:
max(32, CPU cores x 4))

options.name: --keyvalue-workers
options.description:
(Default: 0) Number of
key/value
ephemeral/consistent

options.name: --background-writer-workers
options.description:
(Default: 1) Number of
background writers
workers

options.name: --sequencer-workers
options.description:
(Default: 0) Number of
sequence workers (0 =
auto-size: max(8, CPU
cores))

options.name: --sequencer-block-size
options.description:
(Default: 1000) Values
reserved per sequence
compare-and-swap; one
Raft commit is amortized
over this many values. 1
= gap-free (one commit
per value)

options.name: --sequencer-idempotency-retention-max
options.description:
(Default: 256) Maximum
idempotency entries
retained per sequence
record (0 = no cap)

options.name: --sequencer-idempotency-retention-ttl
options.description:
(Default: 600) Window (in
seconds) within which
retrying a keyed sequence
reserve replays the
identical allocation (0 =
no age pruning)

options.name: --sequencer-max-sequences-per-actor
options.description:
(Default: 10000) Maximum
sequences one actor keeps
resident before evicting
the least recently used
(0 = unbounded)

options.name: --sequencer-block-lease
options.description:
(Default: 5) Seconds a
reserved sequence block
may be served from memory
before it is revalidated
against the durable
record (0 = never
revalidate)

options.name: --default-transaction-timeout
options.description:
(Default: 5000) Default
transaction timeout (in
milliseconds)

options.name: --default-admission-wait
options.description:
(Default: 5000)
Milliseconds a caller
queues for an admission
slot when it does not
request its own budget;
this is the wait to start
a transaction, not the
transaction's lifetime

options.name: --max-admission-wait
options.description:
(Default: 30000) Hard
upper bound (in
milliseconds) on any
admission wait, so no
caller can hold a queue
slot longer than this

options.name: --max-concurrent-transactions
options.description:
(Default: 0) Script
transactions that may
execute concurrently
before further ones queue
and start in priority
order (0 = no limit)

options.name: --max-concurrent-sessions
options.description:
(Default: 0) Interactive
transaction sessions that
may be open concurrently
(0 = no limit)

options.name: --transaction-priority-reserved-slots
options.description:
(Default: 0) Slots out of
each concurrency ceiling
that only high/critical
priority transactions may
occupy

options.name: --transaction-priority-aging-threshold
options.description:
(Default: 1000)
Milliseconds a queued
transaction waits to gain
one effective priority
level (0 = no aging)

options.name: --transaction-priority-max-queued
options.description:
(Default: 4096) Callers
that may wait for an
admission slot per gate
before further ones are
refused retryably (0 =
unbounded)

options.name: --read-io-threads
options.description:
(Default: 4) Read I/O
threads

options.name: --write-io-threads
options.description: (Default: 16) Write I/O

options.name: --backend-read-io-threads
options.description:
(Default: 8) Dedicated
Kahuna backend read pool
threads (point gets,
scans), separate from the
Kommander WAL read pool

options.name: --backend-write-io-threads
options.description:
(Default: 1) Dedicated
Kahuna background-writer
pool threads; the writer
uses a single queue so >1
only adds idle threads

options.name: --backend-read-queue-depth
options.description:
(Default: 4096)
Per-partition
pending-queue depth for
the Kahuna backend read
scheduler

options.name: --raft-enable-shared-executor-pool
options.description:
(Default: true) Share a
bounded pool of worker
threads across all Raft
partitions instead of one
OS thread per partition.
Required to run thousands
of partitions (e.g. after
range splits). Disable
only to isolate scheduler
issues.

options.name: --raft-executor-pool-size
options.description:
(Default: 0) Number of
shared Raft executor
worker threads. 0
auto-sizes to the
processor count. Raise
above the core count only
if ops queue behind busy
partitions while CPU is
not saturated.

options.name: --raft-http-scheme
options.description:
(Default: https://) Raft
HTTP scheme used by REST
communication

options.name: --raft-http-auth-bearer-token
options.description:
(Default: ) Raft HTTP
bearer token used by REST

options.name: --raft-http-timeout
options.description:
(Default: 5) Raft HTTP
request timeout in
seconds

options.name: --raft-http-version
options.description:
(Default: 2.0) Raft HTTP
version used by REST

options.name: --raft-heartbeat-interval
options.description:
(Default: 500) Raft
leader heartbeat interval
in milliseconds

options.name: --raft-recent-heartbeat
options.description:
(Default: 100) Raft
recent heartbeat window

options.name: --raft-voting-timeout
options.description:
(Default: 1500) Raft vote
wait timeout in
milliseconds

options.name: --raft-leadership-barrier-timeout
options.description:
(Default: 10000) How long
a newly elected leader
waits for its promotion
barrier entry to commit
before reverting to
follower, in
milliseconds. Until that
entry commits the node
heartbeats but does not
serve, so raising this
trades failover latency
for tolerance of a slow
quorum

options.name: --raft-leadership-confirmation-timeout
options.description:
(Default: 2000) Maximum
time a read-index
leadership confirmation
may wait for the quorum
ack round plus
applied-frontier catch-up
before failing, in

options.name: --raft-enable-check-quorum
options.description:
(Default: false) When
set, a leader that has
not heard a same-term
append/heartbeat ack from
a majority of voters for
the check-quorum window
steps down to follower

options.name: --raft-check-quorum-interval-multiplier
options.description:
(Default: 8) Number of
heartbeat intervals
without a majority of
same-term acks after
which a leader with
check-quorum enabled
steps down

options.name: --raft-check-leader-interval
options.description:
(Default: 250) Raft
leader check interval in

options.name: --raft-timer-initial-delay
options.description:
(Default: 2500) Initial
delay before Raft timers
start in milliseconds

options.name: --raft-update-nodes-interval
options.description:
(Default: 5000) Raft node
registry update interval

options.name: --raft-start-election-timeout
options.description:
(Default: 2000) Raft
minimum election timeout

options.name: --raft-end-election-timeout
options.description:
(Default: 4000) Raft
maximum election timeout

options.name: --raft-start-election-timeout-increment
options.description:
(Default: 100) Raft
increment in milliseconds

options.name: --raft-end-election-timeout-increment
options.description: (Default: 200) Raft

options.name: --raft-slow-state-machine-log
options.description:
(Default: 50) Raft
state-machine slow
operation log threshold

options.name: --raft-slow-wal-machine-log
options.description: (Default: 25) Raft WAL

options.name: --raft-invariant-checks
options.description:
Reaction when a Raft
consensus invariant check
fails: Off, Log (record
and continue), or Throw
(crash at the offending
transition). Diagnostic
only; never changes
protocol behavior.
Defaults to Throw in a
debug build and Log in a
release build

options.name: --raft-compact-every-operations
options.description:
(Default: 10000)
Committed operations
between automatic Raft
WAL compactions

options.name: --raft-compact-number-entries
options.description:
(Default: 100) Raft WAL
entries removed per
compaction batch

options.name: --raft-max-entries-per-compaction
options.description:
(Default: 5000) Maximum
Raft WAL entries to
process per compaction
run

options.name: --raft-election-timeout-seed
options.description:
(Default: 0) Seed for
deterministic Raft
election timeouts (0 =
random, non-zero =
deterministic; for
testing only)

options.name: --raft-max-queued-client-proposals
options.description:
(Default: 2048) Maximum
client proposals queued
per partition before
backpressure kicks in

options.name: --raft-max-wal-queue-depth-per-partition
options.description:
(Default: 4096)
Per-partition WAL write
queue depth limit

options.name: --raft-max-global-wal-queue-depth
options.description:
(Default: 0) Global WAL
write queue depth limit
across all partitions (0
= unlimited)

options.name: --raft-max-wal-batch-size
options.description:
(Default: 256) Maximum
WAL writes batched per
storage flush

options.name: --raft-max-wal-group-batch-partitions
options.description:
(Default: 64) Maximum
partitions coalesced into
a single WAL
cross-partition
group-commit batch

options.name: --raft-wal-group-commit-linger-ms
options.description:
(Default: 0) Group-commit
linger window in
milliseconds (0 =
disabled; raise on
networks where fsync rate
is the bottleneck)

options.name: --raft-wal-single-fsync-commit
options.description:
(Default: true) Enable
single-fsync fast path:
ack on
propose-quorum-durable
and demote the commit
marker to a lazy write

options.name: --raft-sqlite-wal-shard-count
options.description:
(Default: 0) Number of
SQLite shard databases
across which partitions
are distributed (0 =
resolved to processor
count on first
initialisation)

options.name: --raft-max-drain-quantum-control
options.description:
(Default: 8) Max
control-plane operations
drained per executor wake
cycle

options.name: --raft-max-drain-quantum-replication
options.description:
(Default: 4) Max
replication operations

options.name: --raft-max-drain-quantum-client
options.description:
(Default: 2) Max client
operations drained per
executor wake cycle

options.name: --raft-max-drain-quantum-maintenance
options.description:
(Default: 1) Max
maintenance operations

options.name: --raft-grpc-scheme
options.description:
(Default: https://) URL
scheme prepended to peer
endpoints when opening
gRPC channels

options.name: --raft-grpc-channels-per-node
options.description:
(Default: 4) Number of
pooled gRPC channels
opened to each peer node
(clamped to [1, 64]).
Each channel is a
permanently-held
connection and handler.

options.name: --raft-grpc-enable-multiple-http2-connections
options.description:
(Default: false) Allow
each pooled gRPC channel
to open multiple HTTP/2
connections to spread
concurrent streams

options.name: --raft-grpc-enable-snapshot-compression
options.description:
(Default: false) Compress
Raft snapshot transfers
sent over gRPC

options.name: --raft-snapshot-receive-session-ttl
options.description:
(Default: 30000) How long
an idle snapshot-receive
session is kept before
the receiver discards it
and releases its buffered
bytes, in milliseconds.
Bounds the memory a
leader that vanishes
mid-transfer can strand.

options.name: --raft-snapshot-max-pending-sessions
options.description:
(Default: 8) Cap on
concurrent
snapshot-receive sessions
across all partitions.
Beyond the cap the
receiver evicts its
least-recently-active
sessions.

options.name: --raft-snapshot-max-pending-bytes
options.description:
(Default: 536870912) Cap
on total buffered bytes
across all in-progress
snapshot-receive
sessions. The primary
memory bound on the
receive path.

options.name: --raft-allow-legacy-snapshot-senders
options.description:
(Default: false) Accept
snapshot chunks that
leave the sender's
session-metadata fields
empty, treating them as a
sender that pre-dates
those fields. Temporary
compatibility switch for
a mixed-version cluster.

options.name: --raft-snapshot-transfer-step-timeout
options.description:
(Default: 120000) Upper
bound on one awaited step
of an outbound snapshot
transfer (an export call,
one stream read, or one
chunk send), in
milliseconds. A step that
makes progress resets the
clock; only a step that
stalls trips the timeout.

options.name: --raft-max-pre-auth-request-body-bytes
options.description:
(Default: 33554432)
Ceiling on a Raft REST
request body before it is
authenticated/signed, in
bytes. Bounds buffering
independent of the host's
own request-size limit.

options.name: --raft-backfill-enabled
options.description:
(Default: true) Whether a
leader ships catch-up
batches (and falls back
to a snapshot transfer)
to lagging followers.
Turning it off makes a
follower that misses
entries permanently stale
— only set it false when
the deployment owns its
peers' catch-up story.

options.name: --raft-backfill-threshold
options.description:
(Default: 10) Committed
entries a follower may
trail the leader before
active backfill kicks in

options.name: --raft-max-backfill-entries-per-round
options.description:
(Default: 128) Maximum
committed entries shipped
to a stale follower per
heartbeat interval

options.name: --raft-follower-saturation-backoff
options.description:
(Default: 1000) How long
a leader stops sending
backfill batches to a
peer after that peer
reports its WAL queue
saturated, in

options.name: --raft-backfill-no-progress-pause-cap
options.description:
(Default: 30000) Cap on
the exponential pause
between backfill batches
to a follower whose
reported commit frontier
is not advancing, in

options.name: --raft-backfill-no-progress-anchor-fallback-ships
options.description:
(Default: 2) Consecutive
fruitless backfill ships
after which the leader
re-anchors the next batch
at the follower's
instead of nextIndex.
Values <= 0 disable the
fallback

options.name: --raft-learner-promotion-lag
options.description:
(Default: 10) Maximum
entries a learner may
trail the leader and
still be eligible for
promotion

options.name: --raft-learner-promotion-stable-window
options.description:
(Default: 3000)
Milliseconds a learner
must stay within
promotion-lag before
being promoted to Voter

options.name: --raft-gossip-interval
options.description:
(Default: 5000) Interval
between gossip
anti-entropy rounds in

options.name: --raft-gossip-fanout
options.description:
(Default: 2) Number of
random peers contacted
per gossip round (0
disables gossip)

options.name: --raft-ping-timeout
options.description:
(Default: 500) SWIM
failure-detector ping
timeout in milliseconds

options.name: --raft-indirect-ping-fanout
options.description:
(Default: 2) Number of
intermediary nodes used
for indirect SWIM probing

options.name: --raft-suspicion-timeout
options.description:
(Default: 5000) How long
a node may remain Suspect
before being declared
Dead in milliseconds

options.name: --raft-dead-member-eviction-grace
options.description:
(Default: 30000) Grace
period before a Dead node
is committed as removed
from the roster in

options.name: --raft-self-repair-peer-down-grace
options.description:
(Default: 30000) How long
the promotion-gate
self-repair (gap-skipping
committed drain and
orphaned-tail truncation)
defers while a voter peer
is not Alive, in
milliseconds. 0 disables
the grace

options.name: --raft-ping-interval
options.description:
(Default: 1000) Interval
between SWIM ping rounds
in milliseconds (0
disables the failure
detector). Must be > 0
and <
raft-start-election-timeo
ut when quiescence is
enabled.

options.name: --raft-enable-auto-rejoin
options.description:
(Default: true) A node
that finds itself removed
from the committed roster
(dead-member eviction
firing across a slow
restart) re-runs the join
flow against the
remaining members instead
of staying NotMember.
Disable only when an
operator workflow removes
live nodes and expects
them to stay out.

options.name: --raft-enable-quiescence
options.description:
(Default: true) Quiesce
idle partitions: a leader
stops per-partition
heartbeats after a
partition is idle,
relying on the SWIM
failure detector for node
liveness. Cuts O(NxM)
idle heartbeat traffic
across many partitions.
Requires SWIM
(raft-ping-interval > 0
ut).

options.name: --raft-quiesce-after
options.description:
(Default: 1500) How long
a partition must be idle
(no proposals, no
in-flight replication)
before its leader
quiesces it, in

options.name: --raft-enable-leader-balancer
options.description:
(Default: false) Master
switch for advisory
leader-balancing. When
false (default) no load
reports are built or
gossiped and the balancer
loop never runs. Enable
only after all cluster
nodes support the
feature.

options.name: --raft-leader-balancer-report-interval
options.description:
(Default: 5000) How often
each node emits a load
report on the gossip path
in milliseconds. Shorter
intervals give fresher
data at the cost of more
gossip traffic.

options.name: --raft-leader-balancer-interval
options.description:
(Default: 30000) How
often the P0 leader runs
a balancer planning pass
and dispatches
leader-move suggestions
in milliseconds.

options.name: --raft-leader-balancer-report-ttl
options.description:
(Default: 20000) Maximum
age of a node load report
before it is considered
stale and excluded from
planning in milliseconds.
Must be greater than
raft-leader-balancer-repo
rt-interval.

options.name: --raft-count-deadband
options.description:
(Default: 1) Minimum
leader-count imbalance
above the ideal per-node
count before the balancer
emits any moves. Prevents
flip-flopping around
balanced distributions.

options.name: --raft-load-imbalance-threshold
options.description:
(Default: 0.25)
Fractional load skew
threshold
(maxLoad-minLoad)/maxLoad
between the busiest and
quietest node that
triggers load-tier swaps
when count is already
balanced.

options.name: --raft-min-leader-stability-ms
options.description:
(Default: 5000) How long
a partition must remain
on the same leader (ms)
before it is eligible to
be moved. Prevents
immediate reshuffling of
a partition after an
election.

options.name: --raft-move-cooldown
options.description:
(Default: 60000) How long
a partition is excluded
from further moves after
a transfer suggestion in
milliseconds. Prevents
rapid oscillation on hot
partitions.

options.name: --raft-max-moves-per-pass
options.description:
(Default: 4) Maximum
number of leader-move
suggestions emitted in a
single planner pass.
Limits blast radius of a
bad planning decision.

options.name: --raft-max-concurrent-transfers
options.description:
(Default: 2) Maximum
number of in-flight
transfer suggestions the
P0 leader tracks
simultaneously. No new
moves are dispatched
until outstanding ones
confirm or time out.

options.name: --raft-leader-balancer-ops-weight
options.description:
(Default: 1) Weight of
the EWMA ops/sec term in
the composite
per-partition load score.
Higher values make the
balancer more sensitive
to throughput
differences.

options.name: --raft-leader-balancer-queue-weight
options.description:
(Default: 0.5) Weight of
the instantaneous
queue-depth term in the
composite per-partition
load score. Higher values
make the balancer more
sensitive to pending-work
backlog.

options.name: --raft-suggestion-timeout
options.description:
(Default: 15000) How long
the P0 leader waits for a
suggested move to be
confirmed before
declaring it dropped in
milliseconds. After
timeout the partition is
eligible again subject to
raft-move-cooldown.

options.name: --raft-enable-slow-node-avoidance
options.description:
(Default: false) Master
switch for degraded-node
leader avoidance. When
true, the balancer
classifies nodes whose
WAL commit wait stands
far above the cluster
median as slow, refuses
them as transfer targets,
and drains the
leaderships they already
hold. Acts only inside
the leader-balancer pass,
so it does nothing unless
raft-enable-leader-balanc
er is also true.

options.name: --raft-slow-node-multiplier
options.description:
(Default: 3) How far
above the cluster median
commit wait a node must
sit before it is a slow
candidate. Must be
greater than 1.0.

options.name: --raft-slow-node-floor-ms
options.description:
(Default: 10) Absolute
floor in milliseconds
below which a node is
never a slow candidate,
whatever its ratio to the
median.

options.name: --raft-slow-node-min-samples
options.description:
(Default: 20) Number of
WAL group batches a node
must have observed before
its commit wait is judged
at all. Below this the
node counts as unknown
and is never drained or
excluded.

options.name: --raft-slow-node-observation-ttl
options.description:
(Default: 30000) Maximum
age of a node's last
commit-wait observation
before the node counts as
unknown, in milliseconds.

options.name: --raft-slow-node-enter-passes
options.description:
(Default: 3) Consecutive
balancer passes a node
must look slow before it
is classified Slow.

options.name: --raft-slow-node-exit-passes
options.description:
(Default: 6) Consecutive
clean passes before a
classified slow node is
released. Deliberately
longer than
raft-slow-node-enter-pass
es to avoid flapping.

options.name: --raft-replication-factor
options.description:
(Default: 0) Desired
number of voter replicas
per partition range. 0
(the default) means full
replication: every roster
voter hosts every range.
When > 0, each range gets
a replica set of this
size and quorum is
computed per range over
its voter replicas only.
Prefer odd values.

options.name: --raft-enable-placement-rebalancer
options.description:
(Default: false) Master
switch for the continual
replica-placement
rebalancer on the P0
leader. When false
(default) no rebalancing
moves are planned;
in-flight replica
transitions are still
driven to completion.
Initial placement at
raft-replication-factor
is applied regardless.

options.name: --raft-placement-pass-interval
options.description:
(Default: 5000) How often
the P0 leader runs a
placement-controller pass
(drive in-flight replica
transitions, plan
rebalancing moves) in
milliseconds. Independent
of
raft-leader-balancer-inte
rval: placement runs with
the leader balancer
disabled. A relocation
costs roughly three
passes plus a trim pass,
so this bounds
convergence speed. 0
disables the timer;
commit-driven passes
still run.

options.name: --raft-max-replica-moves-per-pass
options.description:
(Default: 4) Maximum
number of new replica
moves (add or remove
sequences) initiated per
placement-controller
pass, across all
priorities. Bounds the
blast radius of a bad
plan. Keep at least
raft-max-concurrent-repli
ca-repairs plus
ca-transfers, otherwise
it binds first and
starves repairs.

options.name: --raft-max-concurrent-replica-transfers
options.description:
(Default: 1) Maximum
number of ranges with an
in-flight transitional
replica initiated by
balance moves (cosmetic
skew spreading) at any
time. Caps concurrent
backfill/snapshot
transfers so rebalancing
never starves client
traffic. Durability
repair is budgeted
separately by
ca-repairs.

options.name: --raft-max-concurrent-replica-repairs
options.description:
(Default: 3) Maximum
repair moves
(re-replicating
under-replicated ranges
and shedding replicas
stranded on evicted
nodes) at any time. Split
from
ca-transfers so restoring
durability after a node
loss is not serialized
behind the
cosmetic-balance budget.

options.name: --raft-decommission-drain-timeout
options.description:
(Default: 120000) How
long a graceful leave
waits for this node's
replicas to be evacuated
onto survivors before
giving up, in
milliseconds. On expiry
the node is restored to a
voter and the leave
reports DrainTimedOut;
replicas already moved
stay moved, so retrying
resumes the drain. Size
it from the data: an
evacuation costs roughly
three placement passes
per range.

options.name: --raft-replica-count-deadband
options.description:
(Default: 1) Minimum
per-node replica-count
imbalance above the
even-spread ceiling
before the placement
planner emits balancing
moves. Under-replicated
ranges bypass the
deadband.

options.name: --raft-zone
options.description:
Optional locality hint
(zone/rack) for the local
node. When set, the
placement planner prefers
spreading a range's
replicas across distinct
zones.

options.name: --raft-enable-load-reports
options.description:
(Default: false) Gossip
per-partition load
reports even when nothing
else consumes them.
Reports feed the leader
balancer, the placement
planner's zone/leader
hints, and load-based
range splitting; they are
gossiped automatically
whenever the leader
rebalancer, or a
replication factor is
enabled, so this flag
only matters to opt in
without any of those.

options.name: --raft-grpc-enable-append-logs-coalescing
options.description:
(Default: false) Enable
coalescing of multiple
AppendLogs calls into a
single gRPC frame per
write cycle. Useful for
write-heavy
multi-partition workloads
where per-peer send
concurrency is the
bottleneck.

options.name: --raft-grpc-append-logs-max-coalesce-batch
options.description:
(Default: 256) Maximum
number of AppendLogs
items drained into a
write cycle when
coalescing is enabled.

options.name: --raft-transport-security
options.description:
(Default: ) Transport
security and node
authentication settings
(JSON; prefer

options.name: --raft-allow-insecure-cer
options.description:
tificate-validation for
simple dev overrides)

options.name: --raft-max-outbound-queue-bytes-per-peer
options.description:
(Default: 67108864) Cap
on buffered outbound
bytes queued per peer; a
follower that stops
draining has its excess
AppendLogs entries
dropped rather than
accumulated without bound
(dropped entries are
re-shipped by
heartbeat/backfill
retry). 0 disables the
cap.

options.name: --raft-max-backfill-bytes-per-round
options.description:
(Default: 4194304) Byte
cap on a single backfill
round in addition to
raft-max-backfill-entries
-per-round, so a
large-payload workload
cannot materialize an
oversized batch on the
heartbeat path. Also
keeps a batch under the
gRPC receiver's default 4
MB message cap.

options.name: --raft-snapshot-rescue-max-consecutive-cycles
options.description:
(Default: 3) Consecutive
snapshot rescue cycles
that return a
still-below-floor
follower before the
rescue convergence
breaker trips for that
follower. Values <= 0
disable the breaker
(unbounded retries).

options.name: --raft-snapshot-rescue-probe-interval
options.description:
(Default: 300000) While
the rescue convergence
breaker is tripped for a
follower, one rescue
attempt is still allowed
per this interval in
milliseconds, so a
follower whose
environment recovers is
eventually re-seeded.
Values <= 0 disable
probing.

options.name: --raft-snapshot-export-retry-cache-max-bytes
options.description:
(Default: 67108864) Upper
bound in bytes on the
leader-side retry cache
for one produced snapshot
export; an export at or
under this size is cached
and re-sent on retry
instead of re-exported
from scratch. Values <= 0
disable the cache.

options.name: --raft-compaction-live-replica-lag-budget
options.description:
(Default: 100000)
Entry-count budget within
which a follower still
converging after a
snapshot rescue is held
off the WAL compaction
floor, so ordinary
compaction cannot
re-create the below-floor
condition the rescue just
repaired. Values <= 0
disable the hold.

options.name: --script-cache-expiration
options.description:
(Default: 600) Script
cache expiration (in
seconds)

options.name: --revisions-to-cache
options.description:
(Default: 4) Number of
revisions to keep cached
in memory

options.name: --cache-entry-ttl
options.description:
(Default: 1800) Maximum
age of cache entries
before eviction (in

options.name: --cache-entries-to-remove
options.description:
(Default: 100) Maximum
number of cache entries
to remove per eviction
process

options.name: --kv-write-linger-ms
options.description:
(Default: 1) Delay from
the oldest queued direct
write before its
partition batch is
proposed; 0 = immediate
(low-latency escape
hatch)

options.name: --kv-write-max-batch-items
options.description:
(Default: 512) Maximum
log entries per
aggregator Raft call

options.name: --kv-write-max-batch-bytes
options.description:
(Default: 4194304) Target
serialized bytes per

options.name: --kv-write-max-queued-items
options.description:
(Default: 8192) Maximum
admitted direct writes
per partition (incl. in
flight)

options.name: --kv-write-max-queued-bytes
options.description:
(Default: 33554432)
Maximum admitted
partition (incl. in

options.name: --kv-write-max-queue-delay-ms
options.description:
(Default: 1000) Maximum
pre-dispatch residence
for a direct write before
it is released as
MustRetry

options.name: --kv-write-aggregator-inbox-size
options.description:
(Default: 16384)
Ordinary-submission inbox
bound per aggregator lane
(control messages
exempt); <=0 disables

options.name: --dirty-objects-writer-delay
options.description:
(Default: 200) Specifies
how often the dirty
object writer flushes ti
disk (in milliseconds)

options.name: --checkpoint-interval
options.description:
(Default: 30) Period in
seconds at which a dirty
partition checkpoints,
advancing its WAL
retention floor so the
Raft log can compact.
Higher means fewer
checkpoints and a larger
WAL; lower means more
snapshot rewrites.
Default 30.

options.name: --persistent-revision-retention-count
options.description:
(Default: 0) Maximum
persisted key/value
revisions to keep per key
(0 = keep forever)

options.name: --persistent-revision-retention-age
options.description:
(Default: 0) Maximum age
of persisted key/value
revisions in seconds (0 =
disabled)

options.name: --persistent-revision-cleanup-interval
options.description:
(Default: 300) Minimum
interval between full
persistent revision
cleanup sweeps in seconds

options.name: --persistent-revision-cleanup-batch-size
options.description:
(Default: 1000) Maximum
revision records deleted
per cleanup pass

options.name: --persistent-revision-cleanup-on-write
options.description:
Run targeted persistent
revision cleanup after
key/value writes
(default: enabled)

options.name: --disable-persistent-revision-cleanup-on-write
options.description:
Disable targeted
cleanup after key/value
writes

options.name: --pitr-window
options.description:
(Default: 3600)
Point-in-time recovery
window in seconds; WAL
entries older than
now-window may be
compacted. Valid range:
(0, 21600]. Default 3600
(1 hour).

options.name: --base-snapshot-interval
options.description:
(Default: 1800) Interval
between base checkpoints
per shard in seconds.
Must be positive and no
greater than pitr-window.
Default 1800 (30
minutes).

options.name: --pitr-backup-dir
options.description:
(Default: ) Root
directory for PITR backup
artifacts and catalog
manifests. Required when

options.name: --pitr-bootstrap-from
options.description:
Backup ID (GUID) of the
leaf backup to restore
from before joining the
cluster. Must be combined
with --join-existing and

options.name: --pitr-backup-target
options.description:
(Default: local) Which
storage target holds
backups. 'local' (the
default) keeps them under
--pitr-backup-dir on this
host. Any other value
requires the host to
register a backup storage
provider, since
object-storage targets
ship as separate
packages.

options.name: --pitr-backup-scratch-dir
options.description:
(Default: ) Local
directory backup bytes
transit when the target
cannot be written to
directly by the storage
engine. Mandatory for
such a target: a
checkpoint is written
through the filesystem
before upload. Size it
for one whole full
backup, which transits it
in its entirety.

options.name: --pitr-backup-cluster-id
options.description:
(Default: )
Operator-assigned cluster
identity stamped into
every backup manifest;
set the SAME value on
every node. Gates
backup-chain resolution
so a foreign cluster's
artifacts cannot be
chained or restored here.
Empty = unset (guard
dormant).

options.name: --pitr-backup-mac-key-file
options.description:
(Default: ) Path to a
file holding the secret
key that authenticates
backup manifests
(HMAC-SHA-256); set the
same key file on every
node and keep it outside
the backup directory,
readable only by the
server user. When set,
manifests are signed on
write and verified before
restore. Empty disables
authentication. Enabling
it means backups taken
earlier are unsigned and
cannot be restored until
re-taken.

options.name: --backup-retention-max-chains
options.description:
(Default: 0) Backup
retention: keep at most
this many most-recent
backup chains, deleting
older chains whole. 0 =
unbounded. Retention is
off unless at least one
backup-retention-* bound
is set.

options.name: --backup-retention-max-age
options.description:
(Default: 0) Backup
retention: delete any
chain whose newest backup
is older than this many
seconds. 0 = unbounded.

options.name: --backup-retention-max-bytes
options.description:
(Default: 0) Backup
retention: keep the
most-recent chains whose
combined artifact bytes
stay within this budget
(the newest chain is
always kept). 0 =
unbounded.

options.name: --backup-gc-interval
options.description:
(Default: 3600) Cadence
in seconds of the
periodic backup GC pass
(orphan/leftover sweep,
plus retention when
configured); a sweep also
runs shortly after
startup. 0 disables the
periodic pass (GC still
runs inline after each
backup). Default 3600 (1
hour).

options.name: --backup-restore-throttle-mbps
options.description:
(Default: 0) Throughput
budget in MB/s for a
restore's checkpoint
copy, so a restore does
not saturate the disk and
starve foreground
traffic. 0 = unlimited.

options.name: --pitr-restore-root
options.description:
(Default: ) Server-owned
root directory that
restore destinations must
be contained within.
Setting this enables
remote (REST/gRPC)
restore, confining all
targets under this path.

options.name: --pitr-allow-unconfined-remote-restore
options.description:
(Default: false) Allow
remote restore requests
even without a configured
restore root. Insecure;
disabled by default.

options.name: --pitr-backup-dir.
options.description:
omitted the node starts
normally without seeding.

options.name: --pitr-target-time-ms
options.description:
(Default: 0) HLC target
time for PITR restore
expressed as milliseconds
since Unix epoch (the
L/physical component). 0
or omitted means restore
to the chain's natural
maximum (i.e. the full
backup chain).

options.name: --raft-allow-insecure-certificate-validation
options.description:
Skip TLS certificate
validation for inter-node
Raft gRPC connections
(use only in dev/test
environments)

options.name: --range-split-threshold
options.description:
(Default: 1000) Sampled
key count above which a
key range is split
automatically. 0 disables
count-based auto-split
entirely (the checker is
not started). Default
1000.

options.name: --range-split-min-range-size
options.description:
(Default: 10) Minimum
number of keys each half
must hold for an
automatic split to
proceed; guards against
splitting into a range
nothing routes to.
Default 10.

options.name: --range-split-settle-window
options.description:
(Default: 10) Seconds a
freshly split range must
settle before it may be
split again. Must be at
least

options.name: --raft-min-leader-stabili
options.description:
ty-ms, or the new
partition can be re-split
before its leader has
stabilised; startup fails
if it is shorter. Default

options.name: --range-move-settle-timeout
options.description:
(Default: 10) Maximum
seconds a range split or
merge holds its quiesce
while it waits for the
moving range's in-flight
transactions to decide
and settle before the
cutover. Writes into the
moving range are refused
(retryably) for at most
this long per attempt. 0
disables the wait, so a
range under sustained
writes may never split.
Clamped to 15. Default
10.

options.name: --range-merge-min-size
options.description:
(Default: 10) Key count
below which two adjacent
ranges become eligible to
be merged back together.
0 disables auto-merge
not started). Default 10.

options.name: --range-collection-interval
options.description:
(Default: 60) Seconds
between range split/merge
sampling passes. Shared
with the key-value
collector,
prepared-intent recovery
and session range-lock
renewal (whose lease is
twice this interval), so
lowering it to make
splits fire sooner also
shortens those; refused
below the phase-two
commit timeout. Default
60.

options.name: --range-split-load-threshold
options.description:
(Default: 0) Sustained
log-ops/sec above which a
partition becomes a
load-split candidate. 0
disables load-based
auto-split. Cross-node
load signals are only
gossiped when the leader
balancer is enabled, so
without it this is inert
for ranges led elsewhere.
Default 0.

options.name: --range-split-load-min-queue-depth
options.description:
(Default: 8) Minimum WAL
queue depth that must
accompany the ops/sec
rate before a load split
fires; keeps a fast but
unsaturated partition
from splitting. Default
8.

options.name: --range-split-load-window
options.description:
(Default: 15) Seconds the
load predicate must hold
continuously before a
load split is triggered.
Default 15.

options.name: --range-split-load-poll-interval
options.description:
(Default: 5) Seconds
between load-signal
polls. Should stay below
